target_customer: Online shoppers comparing prices on electronics and appliances
problem: Price comparison sites missed the best prices. Bountii crawled merchants more deeply to find lower electronics prices, with plans for more categories.
business_model: Price search engine, likely affiliate or ad revenue; not stated in sources found

founders.name: Samir Meghani
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page. No bio found.

founders.name: John Puskarich
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page. No bio found.

competitors.name: TheFind
competitors.traction_then: Returned the lowest price in TechCrunch's single product test

competitors.name: Google Product Search
competitors.what: Free price comparison over merchant feeds

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed crawling and normalizing prices across more than 30 merchants. Keeping data fresh was the difficult part for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Crowded category with large incumbents and no proprietary data. TechCrunch's single product test found a competitor cheaper.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Product Search and others already offered the same service at launch. No acquisition of Bountii found.

market_need_then: Comparison shopping was an established category in 2007, but TechCrunch's test showed Bountii was not clearly better, so a differentiated need was not shown.

branding.domain_note: bountii.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page, so the domain lapsed
branding.community_and_virality: A TechCrunch launch post dated 2007-10-22 is the only press found.

brand_strength.rationale: One launch article. A bounty pun with a doubled i is easy to confuse with the many Bounty and Bounti brands.

outcome_analysis: Bountii launched on 22 October 2007 into a crowded price comparison market, naming no clear edge beyond crawling more than 30 electronics merchants. TechCrunch's test found a rival cheaper. The company later went inactive and its domain is now for sale. No post mortem was found so the cause is not public; the failure factors are inferred from the competitive landscape and are low confidence.
notes: The $20K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights) whose page text was jumbled, so treat as unverified; no date given. Crunchbase also has a page but the figure was unreadable. Founders' education and employers not found. Failure factors are inferred, not sourced as a stated reason. Dead-site note: bountii.com redirects to a domain sales page.
